passages.note: Bill details page lists Smaltz as author of a bill that itself draws new congressional districts and amends when the general assembly may redraw them.
Smaltz is recorded voting Yea on final House passage of HB 1032, the bill that draws the new congressional districts.

passages.provision_quote: Specifies requirements that apply to any action challenging the apportionment of congressional districts or general assembly districts.
passages.note: As authored, the bill bars temporary restraining orders and stays injunctions pending appeal, but still gives the state supreme court mandatory jurisdiction to hold the apportionment unconstitutional, so it limits but does not remove court review.
passages.actor_quote: Smaltz December 1, 2025, read first time and referred to Committee on Elections and Apportionment.

rows.reasoning: Smaltz authored HB 1032 and voted Yea on its House passage, a bill in which the general assembly itself draws new congressional districts, which rules out an independent or bipartisan commission (rungs 1-3). But the bill's own court-review provisions cut both ways: it bars temporary restraining orders and automatically stays injunctions pending appeal, while still giving the state supreme court mandatory jurisdiction to hold the apportionment unconstitutional, so the record does not separate rung 4's court oversight from rung 5's freedom from outside interference.
needs_source: Smaltz's own statement or floor explanation of HB 1032's court-review provisions tying them to preventing partisan bias (rung 4) or to excluding outside interference (rung 5)
